ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a six-membered cyclic conjugated system, with two π bonds on the left side of the ring, and the same substituted ring/alkenyl carbon on the right side connected to two substituents: above is OSiR3, below is R'. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, indicating that the left-side π electrons migrate along the inside of the ring, and rearrangement/ring opening occurs at the right-side ring bond. Reasoning: According to the arrow-pushing direction, the left-side π bonds shift successively, and the same vinylic carbon on the right side bearing OSiR3 and R' keeps these two substituents unchanged; after the ring skeleton opens, a six-carbon open-chain structure CH2=CH-CH2-CH2-CH=C(OSiR3)-R' is obtained. Writing this product as SMILES, the left terminal alkene is C=CCC, the right-side alkene bond is written according to the stereochemistry shown in the figure as /C=C(O[Si]([*])([*])[*])\[*], and combining them gives C=CCC/C=C(O[Si]([*])([*])[*])\[*].

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: Describe the visual structure first, then label the ring atoms around the cycle, keeping the OSiR3 and R' substituents attached to the same right-hand vinylic carbon. Follow each curved arrow in the image: shift the left-side pi bonds through the ring and open/reassign the right-side ring bond so that the cyclic framework becomes an acyclic six-carbon chain. After electron relocation, the carbon skeleton is CH2=CH-CH2-CH2-CH=C(OSiR3)-R'. Convert this product graph to SMILES: terminal alkene and chain as C=CCC, the right alkene with the depicted stereochemistry as /C=C(O[Si]([*])([*])[*])\[*].
